001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
004import java.time.Instant;
005import java.util.ArrayList;
006import java.util.Arrays;
007import java.util.List;
008import java.util.Locale;
009import java.util.Objects;
010import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;
011import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;
012import java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock;
013
014/**
015 * Alerts (sometimes called errors or status events elsewhere) are for reporting problems
016 * with the logging system itself rather than application logging - for example an
017 * appender failing to write, or an async publisher's queue overflowing. Because logging
018 * itself may be broken these are not routed through the normal {@link LogRouter} but are
019 * instead kept in a small in memory ring buffer (see {@link #dump()} and
020 * {@link #stats()}) as well as immediately reported (currently to stderr).
021 * <p>
022 * An instance is available from every {@link LogConfig#alerts()}. Components that are
023 * {@linkplain LogProvider provided} config, or that are
024 * {@linkplain LogLifecycle#start( LogConfig) started} with config, should prefer
025 * capturing {@code config.alerts()} over reaching for global state.
026 * <p>
027 * {@link LogAlerts} is itself a {@link LogLifecycle}: {@link #start(LogConfig)} is called
028 * exactly once, after every
029 * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} has run, and is
030 * where {@link UnobservedErrorsAction} (already resolved at construction, same as
031 * capacity) gets applied against whatever has been recorded by then - see that enum for
032 * what "nobody is listening yet" means and why it matters specifically at that moment
033 * rather than for the life of the process.
034 *
035 * @see LogConfig#alerts()
036 */
037public sealed interface LogAlerts extends LogLifecycle permits DefaultLogAlerts {
038
039        /**
040         * Default capacity of the alert ring buffer.
041         */
042        static final int DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 128;
043
044        /**
045         * Records an alert.
046         * @param event event describing the alert. {@link Level#ERROR} or higher is expected
047         * but not enforced.
048         */
049        public void error(LogEvent event);
050
051        /**
052         * Records an alert.
053         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
054         * @param throwable cause of the alert.
055         */
056        default void error(Class<?> loggerName, Throwable throwable) {
057                String m = Objects.requireNonNullElse(throwable.getMessage(), "exception");
058                error(loggerName, m, throwable);
059        }
060
061        /**
062         * Records an alert.
063         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
064         * @param message alert message.
065         * @param throwable cause of the alert.
066         */
067        default void error(Class<?> loggerName, String message, Throwable throwable) {
068                var currentThread = Thread.currentThread();
069                error(LogEvent.of(Instant.now(), currentThread.getName(), currentThread.threadId(), Level.ERROR,
070                                loggerName.getName(), message, KeyValues.of(), throwable));
071        }
072
073        /**
074         * A snapshot of the alerts currently held in the ring buffer, oldest first. Alerts
075         * are evicted oldest first once the buffer is at {@link Stats#capacity()}.
076         * @return immutable snapshot.
077         */
078        public List<LogEvent> dump();
079
080        /**
081         * Clears the ring buffer. Does not reset {@link Stats#total()} - like a
082         * Prometheus/Micrometer counter, that is meant to be monotonically increasing for the
083         * life of the process; a downstream metrics system computes rate of change rather
084         * than relying on the counter itself being reset.
085         */
086        public void clear();
087
088        /**
089         * Stats about the alerts recorded so far.
090         * @return stats.
091         */
092        public Stats stats();
093
094        /**
095         * Registers a listener that is notified synchronously, in addition to the alert being
096         * recorded in the ring buffer, every time {@link #error(LogEvent)} is called.
097         * <p>
098         * <strong>Listeners are held with a normal (strong) reference and are not
099         * automatically removed.</strong> This is deliberate: alert listeners are expected to
100         * be few and long lived - typically registered once (e.g. a metrics bridge or an
101         * ops/paging integration) for as long as the owning {@link LogConfig} is - rather
102         * than one per short lived object. A weak reference would risk silently dropping a
103         * listener (a lambda with no other strong reference could be collected almost
104         * immediately) which is the wrong failure mode for something whose entire job is not
105         * losing alerts. Call {@link AutoCloseable#close()} on the returned registration to
106         * unregister deterministically once the caller's own lifecycle ends.
107         * @param listener listener to register.
108         * @return registration; {@link AutoCloseable#close()} unregisters the listener.
109         */
110        public AutoCloseable addListener(Listener listener);
111
112        /**
113         * Notified of alerts as they happen. See {@link #addListener(Listener)}.
114         */
115        @FunctionalInterface
116        interface Listener {
117
118                /**
119                 * Called synchronously every time an alert is recorded. Should not throw -
120                 * exceptions are caught and reported separately so a broken listener cannot
121                 * disrupt alert recording or other listeners.
122                 * @param event the alert.
123                 */
124                void onAlert(LogEvent event);
125
126        }
127
128        /**
129         * Stats about alerts recorded.
130         *
131         * @param total total number of alerts ever recorded, including ones since evicted
132         * from the ring buffer.
133         * @param size number of alerts currently held in the ring buffer.
134         * @param capacity maximum number of alerts the ring buffer holds.
135         */
136        record Stats(long total, int size, int capacity) {
137        }
138
139        /**
140         * What {@link #start(LogConfig)} does if, at that moment, at least one alert has been
141         * recorded and still zero {@link Listener}s are registered - the situation Logback's
142         * {@code StatusManager} calls an unobserved status: nothing is watching, so whatever
143         * went wrong during property loading or a
144         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} would
145         * otherwise only ever have reached the individual, easy to miss stderr lines each
146         * {@link #error(LogEvent)} call already produces.
147         * <p>
148         * Deliberately keyed as
149         * {@value LogProperties#ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY} (an enum, not a
150         * boolean) since "fail" without "dump" first would throw away the only diagnostic
151         * evidence of why it failed.
152         */
153        enum UnobservedErrorsAction {
154
155                /**
156                 * Do nothing beyond what {@link #error(LogEvent)} already does per event.
157                 */
158                NONE,
159                /**
160                 * Default. Report the whole backlog to {@code MetaLog} as one clearly labeled
161                 * block, the same way Logback auto-installs a console listener and prints its
162                 * accumulated status if nothing else is watching by the end of configuration -
163                 * RainbowGum still starts.
164                 */
165                DUMP,
166                /**
167                 * Same reporting as {@link #DUMP}, but then throws, so
168                 * {@link LogConfig.Builder#build()} (and therefore whatever is building a
169                 * {@link RainbowGum} from it) never completes. Goes further than Logback ever
170                 * does - an explicit, opt-in choice of integrity over resilience for deployments
171                 * where a silently-broken bootstrap is worse than refusing to start.
172                 */
173                FAIL;
174
175                static UnobservedErrorsAction parse(String value) {
176                        return UnobservedErrorsAction.valueOf(value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
177                }
178
179        }
180
181}
182
183final class DefaultLogAlerts implements LogAlerts {
184
185        private final LogEvent[] ring;
186
187        private int start = 0;
188
189        private int size = 0;
190
191        private final AtomicLong total = new AtomicLong();
192
193        private final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
194
195        private final CopyOnWriteArrayList<Listener> listeners = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
196
197        /*
198         * Kept apart from listeners.isEmpty() deliberately: DefaultLogConfig's own
199         * metrics-bridge listener (see its constructor) is always registered before
200         * start(...) ever runs, and a passive in-process counter nobody has wired an exporter
201         * to is not "someone is watching" in the sense UnobservedErrorsAction cares about -
202         * only a real addListener(Listener) call (this class's public API) flips this.
203         */
204        private volatile boolean hasExternalListener = false;
205
206        private final LogEventFactory eventFactory = LogEventFactory.of(DefaultLogAlerts.class.getName());
207
208        /*
209         * Resolved once, at construction (same as capacity) rather than inside start(...):
210         * unlike capacity this does not shape any constructor-time state, but LogProperties
211         * is available just as early, and start(LogConfig) is really about announcing "I have
212         * started" (config is there because a few edge cases needed it, not because this
213         * needed to be a start-time lookup).
214         */
215        private final UnobservedErrorsAction unobservedErrorsAction;
216
217        /*
218         * Private and deliberately not defensive - of(LogProperties) below is the only
219         * caller, and it has already validated both fields (capacity > 0, a resolvable
220         * UnobservedErrorsAction) before ever reaching this constructor. Re-checking here
221         * would be defensive programming duplicating what was already a real, reported
222         * validation failure one call up - see of(...)'s own comment.
223         */
224        private DefaultLogAlerts(int capacity, UnobservedErrorsAction unobservedErrorsAction) {
225                this.ring = new LogEvent[capacity];
226                this.unobservedErrorsAction = unobservedErrorsAction;
227        }
228
229        /*
230         * Package-friend static factory: resolves and validates both
231         * LogProperties#ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY and
232         * LogProperties#ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY against one shared Validator
233         * - a mistake in both at once is reported together instead of only the first one
234         * found - then constructs. requirePositiveCapacity is a plain int -> int validating
235         * transform (not an object construction) specifically so it can sit inside map(...)
236         * without tripping CheckerFramework's Initialization Checker, which does not refine a
237         * `new Foo(...)` expression back to @Initialized when it appears directly inside a
238         * lambda body passed through a generic method like map(...) - the one and only `new
239         * DefaultLogAlerts(...)` call stays a plain, unconditional statement here instead.
240         */
241        static LogAlerts of(LogProperties properties) {
242                var validator = LogProperty.Validator.of(LogAlerts.class);
243                var unobservedErrorsActionResult = properties.forKey(LogProperties.ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY)
244                        .ofString()
245                        .map(UnobservedErrorsAction::parse)
246                        .or(UnobservedErrorsAction.DUMP)
247                        .validateIfError(validator);
248                var capacityResult = properties.forKey(LogProperties.ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY)
249                        .ofInt()
250                        .or(LogAlerts.DEFAULT_CAPACITY)
251                        .map(DefaultLogAlerts::requirePositiveCapacity)
252                        .validateIfError(validator);
253                validator.validate();
254                return new DefaultLogAlerts(capacityResult.value(), unobservedErrorsActionResult.value());
255        }
256
257        private static int requirePositiveCapacity(int capacity) {
258                if (capacity <= 0) {
259                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("capacity should be greater than 0");
260                }
261                return capacity;
262        }
263
264        @Override
265        public void error(LogEvent event) {
266                var frozen = event.freeze();
267                total.incrementAndGet();
268                lock.lock();
269                try {
270                        if (size < ring.length) {
271                                ring[(start + size) % ring.length] = frozen;
272                                size++;
273                        }
274                        else {
275                                ring[start] = frozen;
276                                start = (start + 1) % ring.length;
277                        }
278                }
279                finally {
280                        lock.unlock();
281                }
282                for (var listener : listeners) {
283                        try {
284                                listener.onAlert(frozen);
285                        }
286                        catch (Exception e) {
287                                FailsafeAppender.INSTANCE.log(eventFactory.eventNoArg(Level.ERROR, "LogAlerts.Listener threw", e));
288                        }
289                }
290                FailsafeAppender.INSTANCE.log(frozen);
291        }
292
293        @Override
294        public AutoCloseable addListener(Listener listener) {
295                listeners.add(listener);
296                hasExternalListener = true;
297                return () -> listeners.remove(listener);
298        }
299
300        /*
301         * DefaultLogConfig's own metrics-bridge listener goes through this instead of
302         * addListener(Listener) - see hasExternalListener's own comment for why.
303         */
304        void addInternalListener(Listener listener) {
305                listeners.add(listener);
306        }
307
308        @Override
309        public void start(LogConfig config) {
310                if (unobservedErrorsAction == UnobservedErrorsAction.NONE || hasExternalListener || total.get() == 0) {
311                        return;
312                }
313                var backlog = dump();
314                MetaLog.error(eventFactory.eventNoArg(Level.ERROR,
315                                backlog.size() + " alert(s) were recorded before any LogAlerts.Listener was registered - "
316                                                + "dumping the backlog now since nothing else will see it:",
317                                null));
318                for (var event : backlog) {
319                        MetaLog.error(event);
320                }
321                if (unobservedErrorsAction == UnobservedErrorsAction.FAIL) {
322                        throw new IllegalStateException(
323                                        backlog.size() + " alert(s) were recorded before any LogAlerts.Listener was registered and "
324                                                        + LogProperties.ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY + "=FAIL - refusing to start.");
325                }
326        }
327
328        @Override
329        public void close() {
330                listeners.clear();
331        }
332
333        @Override
334        public List<LogEvent> dump() {
335                lock.lock();
336                try {
337                        List<LogEvent> list = new ArrayList<>(size);
338                        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
339                                var e = ring[(start + i) % ring.length];
340                                if (e != null) {
341                                        list.add(e);
342                                }
343                        }
344                        return List.copyOf(list);
345                }
346                finally {
347                        lock.unlock();
348                }
349        }
350
351        @Override
352        public void clear() {
353                lock.lock();
354                try {
355                        Arrays.fill(ring, null);
356                        start = 0;
357                        size = 0;
358                }
359                finally {
360                        lock.unlock();
361                }
362        }
363
364        @Override
365        public Stats stats() {
366                lock.lock();
367                try {
368                        return new Stats(total.get(), size, ring.length);
369                }
370                finally {
371                        lock.unlock();
372                }
373        }
374
375}
